seed_alphas.desc: Continuation proxy: persistent buy-vs-sell aggressor dominance measured by the trend in buy-vs-sell volume stability spread for spread-crossing orders (captures meta-order style persistence).

Continuation proxy on the sell side: increasing instability/shift in sell aggressor flow (via change in sell volume stability) tends to align with short-horizon continuation in the direction of persistent selling pressure.

Interaction proxy for imbalance + order-submission expansion: when spread-crossing flow becomes more buy-dominant while also diverging from overall order submission patterns (SpreadOrder vs OrderLine mean ratio), continuation is more likely.

Mean-reversion gate: low conversion (SpreadOrder_vs_TradeLine.Volume_Mean_Ratio high) coupled with unstable/cancel-like price stability indicates transient impact more likely to revert after the initial move.

Fragmentation indicator: when spread-crossing order volume distribution deviates from executed trade distribution (skew ratio) while price stability in orders changes, it signals unfilled probing and later reversal risk.
Reversion tilt: rising cancel-vs-order skew relative to spread orders suggests low fill efficiency and temporary pressure that tends to mean-revert once liquidity replenishes.

Imbalance proxy via quote-taking pressure: widening divergence between buy and sell price stability for spread-crossing orders reflects directional aggressor pressure that can drive near-term continuation.
Demand shock proxy: a strong trend in spread-crossing value stability (monetary intensity consistency) indicates sustained meta-order execution and short-horizon continuation.

Late reversion proxy: high SpreadOrder-to-Trade mean ratio (low conversion) combined with increasing cancel duration instability implies fleeting liquidity-taking; tends to revert over longer horizons.

Fill-efficiency refinement: divergence between buy-side value in aggressive orders vs executed trades (BuyValue_Mean_Ratio) aligned with changes in buy value stability flags temporary impact and subsequent mean reversion.

Order-submission surge proxy: when SpreadOrder vs OrderLine volume skew ratio rises and is persistent (trend), it indicates a burst of small child orders relative to baseline submissions, supporting short-horizon continuation.

Asymmetry in aggressor informativeness: correlation between buy-side skew divergence (SpreadOrder vs TradeLine) and buy price mean divergence tends to rise when aggressive buys are informative; supports continuation regime identification.
Sell-side low conversion: high sell mean ratio (orders vs trades) with rising sell-side price instability suggests transient selling pressure that later mean-reverts.
Fragmentation proxy: rising cancel-vs-orderline volume skew ratio implies more submitted volume failing to execute; predicts weaker continuation and higher subsequent reversion risk.
Temporal persistence of aggressive flow: higher autocorrelation in spread-crossing order volume stability indicates ongoing meta-order execution, supporting near-term continuation.
Temporal persistence of cancel activity: autocorrelation in cancel volume stability highlights repeated unfilled attempts and liquidity probing; aligns with transient impact and later reversal.
